results.title: Using a Cross-Classified Multilevel Mediation Model (CC ...
results.content: Results show that the proposed method, Cross-Classified Multilevel Mediation Model (CC-M3), outperforms the conventional multilevel model with substantially smaller relative biases in parameter estimates (about 50% less) and a more consistent and higher coverage rate. In subsequent research, a series of simulation studies showed that the confidence interval approach from the residual bootstrapping methods performed well under various conditions in multilevel mediation analysis, such as 2-1-1 and 2-2-1 designs (Pituch et al., Citation2006), 2-1-1 design with nonnormal data (Pituch & Stapleton, Citation2008), and 2-1-1 design with cross- and unique cluster-level mediation (Pituch & Stapleton, Citation2012). Based on the findings from previous simulation studies in multiple membership (Chung & Beretvas, Citation2012) or cross-classified random effects model (Luo & Kwok, Citation2012), we expect that the CC-M3 will outperform the traditional MLM for all the simulation outcomes with a smaller RMSE and bias with a higher coverage rate. The conventional two-level MLM and the CC-M3 were compared in terms of their performance in estimating the direct and indirect effects in mediation modeling.
